question: Where is India’s only confirmed active volcano located, which lies about 135 km south of the Andaman and Nicobar Island's capital, Port Blair?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Barren Island.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Barren Island is part of the** Andaman Islands** group.
 
• It lies on the boundary of the **Indian and Burmese tectonic** **plates**, contributing to its volcanic activity.
 
• It is classified as a **stratovolcano**, characterized by steep slopes and explosive eruptions.
 
• Consideration for **UNESCO World Heritage** status due to its unique geological and ecological characteristics.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Havelock Island:**

 
 
• It is known for its white sandy beaches like **Radhanagar Beach**, which has been ranked as one of the best beaches in Asia.
 
• It is part of the Andaman Islands, rich in marine biodiversity, including **coral reefs **and tropical fish.
 
 
 
• **Wilson Island:**
 
 
• Wilson Island is one of the small and lesser-known islands in the region, not widely associated with volcanic activity.
 
• The island is not a major tourist spot or research area, contributing to its relatively unknown status.
 
 
 
• **Neil Island:**
 
 
• Neil Island is known for its **agriculture**, producing vegetables for the nearby islands.
 
• It is a popular eco-tourism destination with attractions like the natural bridge and **coral reefs**, though less frequented than Havelock Island.
